title: Doodlume full product and presentation audit
disclosure: Simulated perspectives inspired by public work. The named people did not participate, and these comments are not their quotations or endorsements.
brief: Doodlume full product audit, owner asks ANALYSIS, full capability inventory and prioritized plan to improve looks, feel, gameplay and presentation. Do not modify application. Real repo /Users/sreenath/.cache/doodlume-production-source-2026-11-02, current7968fd6. Livehttps://doodlume-production-9df2.up.railway.app. Audience: creators from rough drawings/photos, desktop product review visitors and serious game/product reviewers. Core promise: personal visual material becomes understandable source-faithful play, then creator changes a part/ability without losing the world. Ambition first prize; no guarantees/synthetic ratings. No new mobile push, 3D/world-model detour, generic AI-dashboard theme or removed advanced tools. All recommendations must preserve originals, creative control, old saves/progress and clear authored-vs-generated provenance. Read evidence.json and needed source; screenshots available under /private/tmp/codex-playwright-mcp/full-audit-*.png. Do not operate shared browser. Round1 independent; later read all completed prior rounds. Simulated public-work lens only, not actual people/endorsements. Return ~150–220words substantive public review in contribution contract. Use 1–2 concrete proposals in round1, later no new unless necessary. Write own contribution JSON under contributions/R{n}-{seat}.json, return filename and concise top finding. Never edit others or application. Every factual assertion cite evidence IDs; separate observation/hypothesis/preference.
execution: Ten separate reviewer subagents, one per simulated lens, worked in batches within three concurrent reviewer slots. Each received the same brief/evidence. Round1 was independent; every later round read all completed prior contributions. Primary agent inspected the live desktop product and source, recorded evidence and moderated decisions. No real named person participated. No application code or deployment changed. Mobile refinement excluded under owner preference.

evidence.observation: Owner requires source-faithful varied games, minimal desktop UI, strong craft, no hardcoded scene dispatch, no regressions. Current Ink & Play uses Manrope/Fraunces, cool white, ink, vermilion. Mobile refinement paused.
evidence.limits: A design contract is not proof its implementation is delightful.

evidence.observation: Entire live home inspected top to bottom at1440x900: editorial headline, create/draw actions, rover interactive example with adjacent three-example choices, cat illustration plus three steps, Meta attribution/footer. Examples explicitly authored with AI-generated source art. No actual-photo example on home.
evidence.limits: Screenshot/DOM inspection, not user research. No aesthetic score established.

evidence.observation: Home Draw your own part replaces art on an already-authored rescue part and preserves that ability. It does not infer arbitrary mechanics from that new drawing. Source toggle inspected and worked.
evidence.limits: Prepared example behavior must not be mistaken for general fresh generation.

evidence.observation: Before deliberate Play, no Phaser request observed. After Play, Phaser loaded340920 transfer bytes in322ms in this session. Homepage rover preview transferred338456 bytes. Studio remains mounted hidden after first visit to preserve state.
evidence.limits: One warm/network-specific observation, not a Core Web Vitals or memory benchmark.

evidence.observation: Live create dialog has upload/draw/phone camera, explicit Drawing vs Photo selector default Drawing, optional500character idea, Auto/Adventure/Explore/Hands-on options hidden in Gameplay, disabled Make game explained. Cancelled native chooser opens unchanged draft.
evidence.limits: Fresh actual generation not rerun for audit yet; prior released live request evidence available.

evidence.observation: Runtime supports platform/roam/discover; source-ID actions transfer/attach/use/operate/place; openGate/jumpBoost/moveSpeedBoost/moveObject effects; resources, causal prerequisites, costs, exclusive choices, protected/retryable completion. Bounded2D data-only world:12000x5000,160objects.
evidence.limits: An available primitive is not proof automatic generation uses it engagingly.

evidence.observation: Live example copy opens editor with source-art stage, tool and object selectors, zoom/pan, inspector and Apply footer. Source includes draw/upload object art, movement/size, role/clue, ability forms, source handling, action costs and choices.
evidence.limits: No edits applied in audit; complex inspector usability needs direct inspection.

evidence.source: src/lib/library.ts; shared/revisions.ts; prior released browser checks
evidence.observation: IndexedDB local saves, explicit saves, backup import/export with artwork deduplication/progress/undo history, conflicts handled, progress retained across valid edits. Last release old saved robot reopened/reloaded completed; fresh watering completed/saved/reloaded.
evidence.limits: No cloud accounts, no automatic cross-device sync, no public playable share link evidenced.

evidence.observation: Latest live neutral watering photo compiled source-supported fixed can-to-pot quantity action in51.866s, no review, played/saved/reloaded. Bookshelf local last policy54.833s compiled visual investigation. Initial hosted watering policy had instead chosen a hunt.
evidence.limits: These are selected cases, not success-rate, deep-roleplay or consistent variety proof.

evidence.observation: Occlusion/misrecognition remains. Mug recovered; fragmented fruit and genuinely occluded fruit not solved. Larger segmentation model and permissive crop changes rejected for wrong pixels. Fresh rough robot requested review; exact old/new extraction replay rejected equally.
evidence.limits: No universal object recognition or scene-understanding guarantee.

evidence.observation: 120s interpretation ceiling; one global inFlight interpretation returns429 to concurrent create; per-process paid-attempt allowance; one budgeted same-request503retry; no retry ambiguous timeout/network/billing/auth errors. Numeric-only diagnostics.
evidence.limits: No multiuser queue, fleet-wide quota or latency SLO evidenced.

evidence.observation: Paired phone capture with single-use expiring private link, page alignment, source image updates, model-assisted paper comparison, manual tracing and region correction implemented. Photos use manual update/region flow where automatic comparison is drawing-only.
evidence.limits: Phone physical camera not retested this audit. No AR/world-model reconstruction.

evidence.observation: Local optional recorder captures actual canvas/tab WebM without audio; sound is opt-in, game effects/atmosphere and completion presentation exist.
evidence.limits: Video/narration editor, finished replacement film, listening quality and emotional attachment not established.

evidence.observation: Large orchestration components and overlapping CSS surfaces increase state/style coupling risk. Full release regression suite283checks and type/build/secrets scan passed before audit.
evidence.limits: Line count alone proves neither a defect nor need for rewrite. User explicitly prohibits breaking functionality.

evidence.observation: File upload calls useSource(image,name) and preserves current inputKind; initial default is Drawing. Uploading a JPEG does not automatically select Photo. The picture-vs-drawing choice is consequential to compact photo planning.
evidence.limits: Do not guess input type from MIME alone: JPEGs can depict drawings. Need user-correctable content detection or clearer choice.

evidence.observation: Selected antenna auto-focuses source art and displays Name, Give it a purpose, existing ability, costs/arrangement/add ability, position/size, and world Play style/Choices. New ability opens technical resource/target/amount fields.
evidence.limits: No edits applied. Panel scrolling is intentional; not a proven overflow defect.

evidence.source: Live rover copy public controls; public/art/showcase/rover.json; full-audit-play-action-1440.png
evidence.observation: Played alternate allocation Left→beacon, Middle→rover, Right→beacon, then antenna→rover. Completed Lunar rescue · my version after actual travel. Controls exposed quantities, current held item, next action/unlocked toast; expanded selector panel overlays bottom-right artwork.
evidence.limits: Choice is allocation/order over conserved3units, no scarcity strategy. One browser control wait missed the copy suffix; completion actually succeeded. Screenshot alone does not prove sustained satisfaction.

evidence.observation: ArtworkReview calls every artMethod=sam result a Precise cutout, although source recovery facts explicitly say accepted pixels do not certify semantic identity.
evidence.limits: Code copy concern; screenshot of this label in current review not captured. Recommend wording test without weakening safeguards.

evidence.observation: Official Pulp emphasizes integrated creation/preview and optional deeper scripting. Game Accessibility Guidelines recommend consistent visible interaction signifiers. These support fast creation/play continuity and discoverable source-object actions as design references.
evidence.limits: Neither proves our conversion/retention or recommends copying their visual style. Nintendo PDF search result could not be fetched and is not relied on.

evidence.observation: Rover rule form repeats Power the beacon and Power the rover labels for different source actions. Existing rules and completed states are visible; repeated names make the alternatives harder to distinguish.
evidence.limits: Observed label ambiguity, not evidence that goal validation failed.

evidence.observation: Home had no horizontal overflow at tested sizes. At1920 primarycreation48px,secondarydraw40px,Openstudio44px high. Create dialog at1280 was820x607 positioned230,56.5 withinviewport. Sketch Escape returned to create; focus was Close dialog.
evidence.limits: No full accessibility conformance, mobile, physical device or every inspector-state claim. Sketch opener focus restoration not established.

evidence.observation: Current copied rover world and completed requirements survived home navigation and return. It was in exploration state after opening update tools, so a test looking for the completion heading timed out; snapshot showed3of3 retained.
evidence.limits: Navigation retention is not unsaved-page-reload persistence. Browser work did not alter app source or apply editor/rule changes.

contributions.assessment: Observation: the deliberate-Play Phaser boundary already protects the landing experience [E4]. The more consequential performance problem is creation: selected successful interpretations take about 52–55 seconds, while concurrent requests encounter a process-wide busy gate [E9, E11]. Hypothesis: product review traffic will expose this bottleneck before frontend polish delivers equivalent benefit.
strengths: Preserve deferred Phaser loading and the state-preserving studio lifecycle while measuring their costs [E4].
Save/progress continuity and the existing release checks provide valuable regression anchors [E8, E14].
concerns: A single session resource observation establishes neither Core Web Vitals nor a memory budget [E4].

proposals.action: Introduce a bounded, cancellable creation queue with visible waiting/running states and explicit paid-attempt admission.
proposals.rationale: Preference: preserve originals and avoid duplicate paid retries while making process contention understandable [E11].
proposals.validation: Test simultaneous visitors, cancellation, disconnects and queue saturation; prove one admitted attempt per request and retained drafts/progress. Report queue wait separately from execution latency.

proposals.action: Establish a repeatable desktop performance baseline before extracting narrow editor/session boundaries.
proposals.rationale: Large orchestration surfaces suggest coupling risk, not proof that a rewrite helps [E14].
proposals.validation: Measure cold landing, first Play, repeated studio visits and retained memory; preserve lazy loading, advanced controls, provenance and old-save behavior through the release checks.

contributions.position: Independent first-round recommendation: prioritize trustworthy creation admission, then measure frontend costs before structural changes.
contributions.uncertainty: No concurrent-load or memory benchmark exists in this evidence; capacity and lifecycle costs remain hypotheses [E4, E11].

contributions.assessment: Observation: Doodlume already makes two valuable simplicity choices: deferred game loading and a retained studio that protects an ongoing session (E4). Its rich editing and save model is product value, not evidence that the framework should change (E7, E8, E14). Hypothesis: the next simplification should make state transitions easier to reason about while preserving the creator’s world.
strengths: Explicit saves, revision history and retained progress give creators continuity through edits (E8).
The editor exposes object abilities and source handling as concrete controls (E7).
concerns: Observation: orchestration and styling span large overlapping surfaces; this indicates coupling risk, not a demonstrated defect (E14).
Hypothesis: independent creation, review and editor drafts can become harder to maintain as capabilities grow (E5, E7, E14).

proposals.action: Extract creation and revision sessions behind small typed transition APIs, keeping persistent world/progress separate from temporary drafts.
proposals.rationale: Reduce the number of places that can commit or abandon a draft while retaining every advanced control and save behavior (E7, E8, E14).
proposals.validation: Characterize cancel, review, apply, undo and reopen flows first; preserve old saves and progress across each transition.

proposals.action: Preserve deferred loading; verify that retained, hidden studio sessions suspend gameplay work.
proposals.rationale: Retaining state is useful, but hidden retention deserves lifecycle verification before any performance rewrite (E4).
proposals.validation: Compare idle work before and after a studio visit, then return and verify identical draft and progress.

contributions.position: Prefer incremental ownership boundaries and lifecycle checks over framework migration.
contributions.uncertainty: No measured memory regression or state-transition defect is established; prioritize these changes behind observed creator friction (E4, E14).

contributions.assessment: The browser boundary is promising: deliberate Play defers Phaser, and retaining Studio protects a creator’s working context (E4). I would strengthen measurable responsiveness before adding visual machinery.
strengths: Preserve intentional engine loading and local save/progress continuity (E4, E8).
The existing regression suite provides a useful constraint for incremental delivery (E14).
concerns: The observed transfers are one session; they establish neither cold-load performance nor retained Studio memory cost (E4).
A 120-second interpretation ceiling and one globally admitted request can interrupt a convincing demo; actual frequency remains unknown (E11).

proposals.action: Add a measured browser lifecycle budget for home → Play → editor → home → reopen, preserving the current deferred engine boundary.
proposals.rationale: Retained Studio is a deliberate state-preservation tradeoff; optimize only demonstrated resource costs (E4, E8).
proposals.validation: Measure cold/warm loading, input responsiveness, retained heap and hidden-page activity across repeated cycles; verify drafts and completed saves survive. Set budgets from the baseline.

proposals.action: Make long creation and server-busy recovery explicit: truthful status, draft-preserving exit, and deliberate retry after a busy response.
proposals.rationale: The admitted-request limit and bounded retries warrant a designed recovery path; no new queue is assumed (E11).
proposals.validation: Exercise concurrent creation and timeout cases; confirm understandable recovery, retained artwork/idea, and no automatic duplicate paid attempt.

contributions.position: Prefer incremental lifecycle and recovery work over framework migration.
contributions.uncertainty: No fresh performance trace or concurrency usability test supports a quantified speed or reliability claim (E4, E11).

contributions.assessment: Observation: the desktop editor gives artwork most of the space and retains precise native controls; this is a sound foundation for creative control (E7). Hypothesis: its initial empty inspector makes discovering a meaningful first edit harder than discovering pan and zoom (E7).
strengths: Source art, object selection and an explicit Apply boundary make authorship tangible (E7).
Backup and retained progress support experimentation without abandoning an existing world (E8).
concerns: The inspected initial editor shows a prominent view toolbar but only ‘Select an object to edit’ in the inspector; the relationship between object, ability and play remains implicit (E7).
Overlapping style surfaces warrant bounded changes and regression checks, not a rewrite justified by size (E14).

proposals.action: Give the empty inspector a concise first-edit invitation and offer selecting the character; after selection expose the current ability and a short keyboard-help disclosure.
proposals.rationale: Preference: teach the edit-to-play relationship at the point of action while retaining advanced controls (E7).
proposals.validation: Observe desktop visitors selecting an object, changing one ability, applying and replaying; verify keyboard focus visibility, selection, movement, cancellation and retained progress directly.

contributions.position: Preserve the artwork-led desktop layout and explicit Apply boundary (E7).
contributions.uncertainty: Screenshot and source inspection do not establish keyboard usability, assistive-technology behavior or accessibility conformance (E7).

contributions.assessment: Observation: the homepage already has an identity worth extending: artwork dominates, editorial typography supplies character, and vermilion identifies creation. The editor shares its quiet surfaces but introduces substantially denser controls; consistency should make that transition understandable rather than flatten both surfaces into one layout. [E1,E2,E7]
strengths: Selected examples combine a border, check and explicit Selected text; this is a useful reusable selection pattern. [E1,E2]
The design contract distinguishes creation, Play, focus, selection and errors instead of assigning every state one brand color. [E1]
concerns: Hypothesis: overlapping stylesheet surfaces increase the chance that future controls drift in size, focus or disabled treatment. File size alone does not establish a current user-facing defect. [E14]

proposals.action: Document and incrementally consolidate the existing button, selection, field and disclosure patterns into shared primitives, beginning with create and editor; preserve the established typography and palette.
proposals.rationale: A small component vocabulary makes advanced tools feel related without removing capability or undertaking a risky rewrite. [E1,E7,E14]
proposals.validation: Compare default, hover, focus, selected, disabled and error states at the three documented desktop sizes; exercise create cancellation, editor Apply/Discard and saved-world return before each migration.

contributions.position: Preserve Ink & Play; prioritize repeatable interaction states over a new visual theme. [E1]
contributions.uncertainty: Screenshot review does not establish keyboard accessibility, inspector usability or observed confusion; validate these directly. [E7]

contributions.assessment: Observation: the homepage already has a convincing hierarchy: oversized mixed typography, a restrained vermilion action, and generous space around the playable artwork [E1,E2]. My preference is to carry that compositional confidence into the working tools.
strengths: The example picker separates navigation from the stage; source-art attribution stays present without competing with Play [E2].
The create dialog visibly separates required image input from the optional idea and explains its disabled action [E5].
concerns: The editor screenshot gives a small empty inspector and collapsed controls similar pale bordered containers; the next useful action has little visual emphasis [E7].

proposals.action: Give the editor inspector a clear object heading, a useful empty-state instruction, and stronger spacing between object properties and world rules; retain advanced controls.
proposals.rationale: Preference: use hierarchy to expose scope without adding decoration [E7].
proposals.validation: Compare unselected and selected screenshots at 1440×900; ask creators to locate art replacement and ability editing.

contributions.position: Preserve the homepage typography and stage-first layout; concentrate visual refinement on the editor [E1,E2,E7].
contributions.uncertainty: Hypothesis: clearer inspector hierarchy reduces search effort. No selected-object screenshot or usability timings establish that effect yet [E7].

contributions.assessment: Observation: creation already has a sensible primary task: supply an image, optionally describe an idea, then make a game; gameplay choices are disclosed progressively (E5). My hypothesis is that the bigger friction is uncertainty about what that action will produce and how long it will occupy the visitor, rather than too many visible fields (E5, E9).
strengths: Preserve optional intent, collapsed gameplay controls, explained disabled submission, and retained drafts after cancellation (E5).
Preserve the source-art editor and its advanced controls; creative revision is part of the promise (E7).
concerns: The homepage supplies authored drawing examples but no actual-photo example; a photo creator must infer applicability (E2).
Selected photo generations took approximately 52–55 seconds, while capability does not establish reliable outcomes across inputs (E9, E10).

proposals.action: Add one clearly labeled actual-photo example with its original, resulting action, and provenance beside the existing examples.
proposals.rationale: Demonstrate the task visitors can accomplish while distinguishing prepared replacement-art behavior from fresh generation (E2, E3).
proposals.validation: In desktop sessions, ask photo creators to explain the expected output and identify authored versus generated material before creating.

proposals.action: Test concise pre-submit expectation copy and truthful creation progress, retaining image and idea through recovery.
proposals.rationale: Reduce uncertainty during evidenced long waits without adding mandatory form steps (E5, E9).
proposals.validation: Observe desktop first-create abandonment, expectation accuracy, and successful recovery; do not display fabricated stage completion or timing guarantees.

contributions.position: Prefer improving confidence along the existing creation path before adding onboarding steps; mobile remains paused (E1).
contributions.uncertainty: No first-use study or representative generation success rate is available (E9, E10).

contributions.assessment: Observation: Doodlume's strongest product promise is continuity: recognizable source material becomes play, then changes without losing progress (E7–E9). Hypothesis: visitors will judge that promise through the first meaningful decision, not the number of creation tools.
strengths: Source-stage editing and retained progress make authorship tangible rather than disposable generation (E7, E8).
Costs, prerequisites and exclusive choices provide ingredients for consequential play (E6).
concerns: The homepage's replacement-art interaction preserves an authored ability; its immediate success could imply broader inference than it demonstrates (E3).
Selected watering and bookshelf successes establish feasibility, while the earlier watering hunt shows that activity selection can weaken source meaning (E9).

proposals.action: Make the first-session arc explicit: recognize the source, understand a goal, make one consequential choice, see its result, then edit and replay. Name prepared-example authorship beside the interaction.
proposals.rationale: Preference: one coherent learning arc should connect the existing example, gameplay and editor capabilities (E2, E3, E6, E7).
proposals.validation: Observe first-time visitors explaining the source-to-action relationship and predicting what their edit changes before replay.

proposals.action: Evaluate generated games on source relevance, consequential decisions and feedback; retain repair/review when recognition is uncertain.
proposals.rationale: Hypothesis: generation completion alone misses whether play expresses the submitted material (E6, E9, E10).
proposals.validation: Blind-review varied fresh drawings/photos; record goal comprehension, meaningful choices and unsupported mechanics separately.

contributions.position: Prioritize a complete creator-to-player experience before adding more surface features.
contributions.uncertainty: No fresh generation or participant testing was performed for this contribution; engagement remains a hypothesis (E9).

contributions.assessment: The brand has a credible center: an editorial invitation wrapped around visibly personal material. Preserve Ink & Play. The restrained ink/vermilion frame lets the artwork carry the imagination; that is my art-direction preference, supported by the existing contract and inspected homepage, not a measured conversion advantage (E1, E2).
strengths: The rough pencil cat gives the promise a human scale alongside the spectacular rover; explicit authored-example provenance earns trust (E2).
The editor keeps source artwork prominent while exposing practical controls, extending the product beyond a decorative demo (E7).
concerns: The homepage promises drawings and photos but offers no actual-photo example. That is an observed evidence gap; visitors distrusting photo capability is a hypothesis (E2, E9).
The strongest creative claim concerns changing play, but the homepage drawing interaction preserves a prepared ability. Its framing needs equal precision (E3).

proposals.action: Add one verified actual-photo source-to-play case within the existing example presentation, with original source and provenance.
proposals.rationale: Make the advertised input range visible without diluting the established art direction.
proposals.validation: Visitors identify which case used a photograph and describe its source-supported action.

proposals.action: Clarify the prepared example's drawing step as replacing a part's appearance while retaining its ability.
proposals.rationale: Match the creative invitation to demonstrated behavior.
proposals.validation: Visitors distinguish appearance replacement from inventing a new mechanic.

contributions.position: Preserve the visual identity; strengthen its proof and wording.
contributions.uncertainty: Screenshots and source cannot establish comprehension, delight, or brand preference across audiences.

contributions.assessment: Through a simulated Susan Kare-inspired visual communication lens, the homepage communicates invitation clearly: a labeled play button, pictorial examples, and a selected checkmark make the next action legible (E2). The editor is less self-explanatory: its beautiful source scene dominates while the empty inspector says only ‘Select an object to edit’ (E7).
strengths: Text accompanies key homepage symbols; selection uses both a border and checkmark (E2).
The editor preserves source artwork as the central visual reference (E7).
concerns: Hypothesis: newcomers may read the editor scene as a flat image before discovering selectable objects (E7).

proposals.action: Add an optional ‘Show editable objects’ overlay with restrained contours and names; link canvas hover, keyboard focus, object selector, and inspector selection.
proposals.rationale: Make editing affordances visible without replacing personal artwork (E7).
proposals.validation: Ask first-time desktop creators to select and rename one existing object; observe discovery and mistaken clicks, then verify overlay-off artwork fidelity.

proposals.action: Keep ‘Draw your own part,’ but add ‘Keeps this part’s rescue ability’ beside its entry point.
proposals.rationale: The icon promises drawing; adjacent words should explain the actual preserved mechanic (E3).
proposals.validation: Before drawing, ask visitors what will change; check that they predict artwork replacement and retained ability.

contributions.position: Prioritize readable object affordances and accurate action labels over additional decorative icons.
contributions.uncertainty: Screenshots and source inspection establish presentation and behavior, not measured misunderstanding or task success (E2, E7).

contributions.assessment: Observation: the evidence establishes long selected executions and a single-process admission gate, but no arrival-rate distribution [E9, E11]. I therefore qualify my queue recommendation: clearer recovery is immediately reviewable; a queue is a capacity experiment, not a prerequisite for a trustworthy demo.
strengths: Rich’s recovery proposal preserves drafts and avoids automatic duplicate paid work [E5, E11].
concerns: Hypothesis: a queue can merely convert an explicit busy response into several minutes of invisible waiting; serial service remains serial [E9, E11].

responses.comment: Adopt truthful busy/timeout recovery first. Counterexample to my initial queue preference: if several visitors submit together, retaining every request can prolong the least predictable portion of first use. Test contention and abandonment before choosing bounded admission [E9, E11].

Support lifecycle checks before session extraction. A hidden studio that preserves drafts is valuable; extracting it solely because files are large adds migration risk without a demonstrated performance gain [E4, E8, E14]. Characterize cancel/apply/reopen first, then extract only boundaries implicated by observed failures.

contributions.position: Change P-r1-addy-1 from immediate implementation to a deferred, measured queue experiment after Rich’s recovery work. Maintain P-r1-addy-2 as measurement before refactoring; consolidate its lifecycle baseline with Rich and Evan.
contributions.uncertainty: No concurrent usability study, queue demand estimate, memory trace or latency distribution supports a queue-size or resource-budget number [E4, E11].

contributions.assessment: Preference: take the smallest change that makes creation recovery trustworthy, then measure whether stronger admission machinery is justified. Observation: selected generations already occupy roughly a minute, and concurrent creation receives 429; the evidence establishes contention mechanics, not its frequency among visitors (E9, E11).
strengths: Rich’s recovery path preserves the existing interaction while addressing the admitted-request limit (E5, E11).
Lea’s first-edit invitation respects the editor’s explicit Apply boundary and advanced capabilities (E7).
concerns: Hypothesis: introducing a queue immediately multiplies states involving waiting, cancellation, disconnect and paid admission before demand is measured (E11).

responses.comment: Support the admission concern, but challenge queue-first sequencing. Ship truthful busy recovery and retained drafts first; use observed simultaneous demand to justify queued-job ownership and cancellation semantics. A queue cannot itself shorten interpretation (E9, E11).

Support a first-edit invitation before restructuring the inspector. Keep selection state shared between stage and inspector, and preserve explicit Apply/Discard behavior; capability removal would undermine creative revision (E7, E8).

contributions.position: Maintain both R1 proposals, but place session extraction after recovery and editor comprehension work. Extract only boundaries touched by those changes; file length alone does not justify a broad refactor (E14).
contributions.uncertainty: No concurrency frequency, cancellation study or selected-inspector task test establishes the best implementation scope. Queue adoption and inspector restructuring remain conditional (E7, E11).

contributions.assessment: My priority remains predictable creation recovery and measured browser lifecycle work. The council should distinguish a known admission limit from an unmeasured claim about audience-scale failure (E11).
strengths: Addy and Evan both preserve deferred loading and treat retention as a tradeoff requiring measurement (E4).
The existing save and progress behavior supplies concrete regression expectations (E8).
concerns: A queue can turn an immediate busy response into an indefinite-feeling wait; the evidence gives no arrival-rate distribution or operational queue requirement (E9, E11).

responses.comment: Support explicit admission and draft retention, but test busy recovery first. A bounded queue deserves a separate evidence gate: demonstrate concurrent demand, define maximum wait and cancellation semantics, and prove admission does not multiply paid attempts. The selected 52–55-second runs cannot establish useful queue capacity (E9, E11).

Support typed transition boundaries after characterizing behavior. Do not couple extraction to performance claims: large files establish coupling risk, while no retained-memory defect is evidenced (E4, E14). Ship a narrow extraction only when it simplifies a demonstrated transition without weakening save continuity (E8).

contributions.position: Maintain lifecycle baselines and truthful recovery as immediate work; treat queuing as a conditional experiment and architectural extraction as subsequent, bounded maintenance.
contributions.uncertainty: Neither concurrent-load traces nor cold-load, hidden-work or heap measurements exist in the supplied evidence (E4, E11).

contributions.assessment: An editable-world aid should explain selection without becoming a second illustration. The inspected stage is already visually detailed, while an object selector provides a separate route into editing (E7). My preference is a reversible discovery aid, with the selected object's ability visible once chosen.
strengths: The existing object selector and Apply boundary give the proposed guidance concrete controls to connect (E7).
Preserved progress makes a small editing experiment credible (E8).
concerns: Hypothesis: names and contours for every editable object could obscure the source scene, particularly where recognition already fragments objects (E7, E10).

responses.comment: Support an optional overlay, but treat a crowded or fragmented scene as the counterexample to showing every contour and name simultaneously (E7, E10). Begin with a restrained hover/focus or selected-object treatment; test the all-objects aid as a deliberate toggle, with the native selector equally discoverable.

Retained studio state is useful evidence against remounting the editor merely to simplify lifecycle ownership (E4, E8). Verify suspended hidden work while preserving draft selection, focus-return intent and progress.

contributions.position: Maintain P-r1-lea-1: simplify the invitation and hierarchy, not the available abilities. Coordinate it with Susan's selection aid and Steve's inspector hierarchy (E7).
contributions.uncertainty: These are design hypotheses; no keyboard task trial, selected-object usability study or hidden-work measurement establishes the preferred treatment yet (E4, E7).

contributions.assessment: Consistency should preserve different task rhythms. The art-led homepage and denser editor are already intentionally distinct; shared tokens should govern meaning and state, while layout and disclosure follow the task. [E1,E2,E7]
strengths: The documented distinction between creation and Play is a useful boundary against indiscriminate component uniformity. [E1]
concerns: Hypothesis: consolidating styles before observing a selected-object editing task could preserve the wrong hierarchy in a cleaner implementation. The current evidence does not establish a state defect. [E7,E14]

responses.comment: Your first-edit invitation is a stronger immediate intervention than a broad primitive migration. Teach selection and current ability in the existing inspector, then extract only patterns proven useful through that task. [E7]

Agree on distinguishing object properties from world rules, but do not make every panel visually prominent. Give the selected object the heading and reserve stronger emphasis for the next actionable control; keep advanced world settings available through disclosure. This is a hierarchy preference to test. [E7]

Typed ownership and component consistency can cooperate, but neither needs to precede the targeted inspector improvement. Couple a style extraction to its own Apply/Discard and saved-world checks rather than bundle state and CSS refactors. [E8,E14]

contributions.position: Maintain P-r1-brad-1 as P2 groundwork; sequence observed first-edit craft and verification ahead of consolidation. Preserve the palette, fonts and contextual density. [E1,E7]
contributions.uncertainty: Selected-object screenshots and direct creator observation remain absent; no measured search-time improvement is established. [E7]

contributions.assessment: The main visual tension is evidence versus density. Observation: three examples already flank a dominant stage, while the source-to-play photo promise lacks an actual-photo case [E2]. Preference: strengthen proof inside that composition before adding another promotional section.
strengths: The existing picker and source toggle provide a presentation structure for provenance [E2,E3].

Change source-kind clarity first, then truthful creation recovery and a bounded first-edit invitation; these address the task before broader polish (E11, E15, E16).
strengths: The completed rover loop demonstrates usable source objects and visible causal feedback; small agency is already a credible foundation (E17).
concerns: Avoid treating additional branches, scarcity or compulsory review as evidence of better gameplay. Selected generation and completion cases establish feasibility, while recognition failures remain real (E9, E10, E17).

responses.comment: Adopt your preview-adjacent Drawing/Photo choice. Acceptance: creators distinguish an ordinary photo from a photographed drawing, predict interpretation, and retain intentional choice through replacement and reopening; file format must not decide content (E15).

Your narrowed agency standard resolves our gameplay tension. Acceptance should test source recognition, predicted action and understandable outcome, followed by one supported edit and replay with progress retained (E8, E16, E17).

contributions.position: Maintain both R1 proposals as one coherent-experience evaluation. Residual dissent: no universal minimum branch count or mandatory tutorial; preserve small faithful games and condition repair on uncertainty.
contributions.uncertainty: No participant study or representative generation sample supports claims about delight, retention or reliable variety. Gameplay acceptance requires fresh mixed-input evaluation, not showcase completion alone (E9, E10, E17).

contributions.assessment: Preserve Ink & Play's editorial typography, restrained palette and artwork-led stage; this is a coherent art-direction preference grounded in the current contract and presentation, not a measured superiority claim (E1, E2). Change first the promise-to-proof details: explain the consequential source-kind choice, state retained ability beside drawing replacement, and describe automatic cutouts without semantic certainty (E3, E15, E18).
strengths: Selected-object editing and demonstrated source-supported play provide a credible product story beyond generated imagery (E16, E17).
concerns: Avoid presenting one photo success as general reliability or alternate allocation as scarcity strategy (E9, E17).

responses.comment: Your source-kind correction belongs before cosmetic expansion. Acceptance: creators distinguish an ordinary photo from a photographed drawing, retain intentional overrides, and predict the chosen interpretation without another onboarding screen (E15).

Accept your agency criterion. A small action can carry the brand if visitors recognize its source, predict its effect and understand completion. No branching-depth requirement follows from the observed rescue (E17).

contributions.position: Maintain both original proposals with the photo case rotating within the current stage footprint. Accept when visitors identify original/provenance, explain the real action and find Play; preserve existing saves, progress and ability controls (E2, E8, E16). My remaining dissent is against expanding homepage density before testing that compact presentation.
contributions.uncertainty: Photo-proof placement and copy changes need participant comparison; no evidence establishes conversion gain or sustained delight (E2, E9, E17).

contributions.assessment: Preserve the artwork-led frame, labeled actions and existing selector-to-inspector connection (E2, E16). Change first the wording that defines trust: clarify retained rescue ability and replace the certainty implied by ‘Precise cutout’ (E3, E18). These are agreed recommendations to test, not demonstrated comprehension improvements.
strengths: Existing selected identity, current ability and auto-focus already support orientation; retain them while checking keyboard return and focus (E16).
concerns: Avoid permanent all-object labels or duplicated ability headings without observed discovery failures. Artwork already competes with an expanded play selector in one evidenced state (E16, E17).

responses.comment: Accept your stronger acceptance criteria: a keyboard creator selects an object, identifies its ability, edits, applies and returns; Discard preserves the prior world and progress (E8, E16). This test should decide whether guidance is needed before my overlay proceeds.
Prioritize the understandable Drawing/Photo choice beside the preview; a consequential mode deserves visible words and retained user choice, never a format-based guess (E15).

contributions.position: Adopt concise retained-ability clarification; test Automatic cutout wording; defer the optional overlay until direct selection failures justify it. My dissent is against treating visible interaction guidance as synonymous with more persistent labels.
contributions.uncertainty: Accept wording when creators predict appearance versus ability change and understand cutout uncertainty. Accept guidance only after comparative desktop tasks; no supplied study establishes either improvement (E3, E16, E18).

assessment: The strongest product is recognizable personal visual material made consequential and editable without losing the world. Existing composable2D capabilities outpace automatic design consistency.
Engine validity, source extraction, visual craft, engaging play and presentation must be assessed separately. No perfect score or competitive superiority follows from this review.
preserve: Keep the artwork-first stage, Ink & Play typography/palette, concise creation path and optional advanced tools.
Preserve actual Meta inference, source pixels, strict ID/geometry validation, creator overrides, deterministic rules, old saves, revision identity and earned progress.
Retain deferred Phaser loading, explicit audio activation, keyboard alternatives, original-source inspection and transparent example provenance.
critical_issues: No new demonstrated critical functionality break identified during this audit. Major source-kind comprehension issue: upload retains Drawing although Photo changes planning.
Major product weakness: unfamiliar inputs can require outline correction or generate shallow investigations; selected successful watering is not broad roleplay proof.
Precision wording overstates accepted SAM output; fix claims without relaxing cutout validation.
Concurrent generation is single-process/single-flight; meaningful contention and latency distribution remain unmeasured.
visual_direction: Preserve the existing coherent brand; no evidence supports another palette/font reset. Improve task hierarchy, control states and scene-safe contextual feedback.
Keep the original art dominant; selected-object inspector already has identity and existing ability, so do not duplicate them. Test first-selection invitation and clearer rule-authoring language.
Integrate real-photo proof within the current chooser by replacement/rotation; avoid additional homepage density until tested.
Inspect typography, spacing, focus/selection, disabled/busy/error/success states at the three desktop sizes; observed screenshots alone do not certify aesthetics.
ux_content: Clarify Drawing/Photo beside the uploaded preview with retained override. Do not guess input type from MIME.
Describe home part drawing as changing art while retaining an authored ability, not arbitrary mechanic inference.
Use neutral Automatic cutout wording and preserve correction access.
Explain resource/action relationships plainly; source→verb→target naming can distinguish repeated alternatives.
Creation cancellation, waiting and recovery need truthful concise feedback with preserved image/idea and deliberate retries.
frontend_performance: No Phaser request before deliberate Play observed; one firstPlay engine transfer340920bytes/322ms is session-specific, not a benchmark.
Measure home→play→editor→home→return lifecycle, hidden activity and repeated-session memory before teardown or architectural changes.
Large App/editor/CSS sizes indicate potential coupling, not proof of failure. Extract narrow boundaries only when validated UX changes require them.
Queue implementation is conditional; start with understandable busy handling and measured demand.
agreements: All ten perspectives preserve artwork, existing creative power and state continuity; no one endorses a framework migration or wholesale theme reset.
Reviewers revised initial inspector proposals afterE16 showed name and ability already exist.
Photo proof belongs in the existing stage/chooser rather than another marketing section.
Small faithful gameplay can show agency; arbitrary scarcity, chores and prerequisites should not manufacture depth.
disagreements: Queue-first proposal was deferred after cross-examination: contention risk is real but frequency and queue benefit are unmeasured.
Optional editable-object contours remain a possible experiment, not an adopted default; existing selection cues already work and busy sources may become cluttered.
State extraction and component consolidation remain conditional on actual change pressure; measure and preserve behavior before migration.
sequence: M0 audit complete; M1 review coherent critical-state visual treatment.
M2 clarify creation intent/source type and recovery; M3 improve source-specific automatic activity quality.
M4 simplify meaningful invention; M5 strengthen causal game feel and readable rules.
M6 verify varied fresh inputs, old saves and desktop states throughout; M7 present verified photo/drawing proof within the homepage.
validation: Use complete source→interpret→review(if needed)→play→edit→undo→save→reopen sessions. Count attempts, reviews, failures and actual completions separately.
Observe goal comprehension and ability prediction with first-time creators; no representative user study was performed here.
Verify every UI increment at1280x720,1440x900,1920x1080, preserving keyboard paths, original art and precise advanced controls.
Set latency/frame/lifecycle budgets from measured baselines; report hardware/network and distribution, not only selected best runs.
Require source-kind choice, correct labels, accessible status and stable state on cancel/busy/timeout; run relevant existing regressions, type/build/secret checks.
limitations: Desktop browser and source audit with prior released inference evidence; no fresh inference performed in this audit.

Current audit exercised rover allocation/attachment completion and navigation retention, create/sketch Escape, source toggle, selected editor, rules, update and empty library; it did not re-test every inventory feature.
No external judges, actual celebrity review, physical phone-camera test, sound listening, screen-reader certification, user retention study or complete arbitrary-input validation.
External referencesPulp and GameAccessibilityGuidelines inform principles only; unavailable NintendoPDF was not relied upon.
